specName: One Language for Every Tool Type
approach: ATD is specified in specifications/atd/ as one strict LALR(1) grammar in a stated subset of Lark notation, with soft keywords, CEL inside the grammar and a bounded deterministic script. It is implemented once, in Rust crates of the desktop host, whose language server runs in process there, as WebAssembly in VS Code and as a native binary under IntelliJ's LSP API. A validation runtime lowers descriptions onto the desktop host's existing engines and replays fixtures built from the standalone goldens.

decisions.decision: Implement parser, checker, script, runtime and language server once, in Rust, in etalii.adp.ide.desktop
decisions.why: FR-043 and FR-054 ask for one runtime and identical diagnostics; the desktop host is Rust and has the engines
decisions.rejected: a checker per host; a Python checker in etalii.adp; TypeScript shared core

decisions.decision: VS Code runs the language server as wasm32 WebAssembly inside the universal vsix; IntelliJ runs native binaries through the optional com.intellij.modules.lsp
decisions.why: one implementation, each host its own mechanism, one vsix, no extra plug-in

decisions.decision: One grammar table for all kinds, kind admission in the checker; soft keywords under a contextual lexer
decisions.why: conflict-free shared core (FR-004), keywords usable as names (FR-008), refusals at the construct
decisions.rejected: a grammar per kind; reserved keywords with escapes

decisions.decision: Conformance bytes from the standalone goldens vendored in the desktop host; readings and drawings recorded from the desktop host at fe5feec
decisions.why: the standalone host is out of scope and the desktop host already proves byte parity with it
decisions.rejected: a new recorder in the standalone host; screenshot drawings

decisions.decision: etalii.adp Build builds the Rust checker from the same-named desktop branch, else develop
decisions.why: FR-100 needs the full checker and language and checker change together
decisions.rejected: a pinned released binary (release cycle between repositories)

decisions.decision: The validation runtime lowers descriptions onto adp-disl, adp-desl, adp-fbl, adp-scene and adp-diagram with generic extension points
decisions.why: parity by default; no fourth DISL implementation in one host

plan.summary: ATD 0.1 planned: grammar, script and capabilities in etalii.adp, one Rust toolchain in the desktop host serving every IDE, 36 tool descriptions with traces and fixtures, FBL 0.9 grammar family
